main_text.p: A Thenis, celeberrimæ cui civitati ac Reipublicæ omnium artium ac disciplinarum, natales & incunabula debentur, moris fuisse ex antiquitate constat, ut, qui magnis vellet imbui mysteriis, quod aliquandiu nemini licebat, parvis ante imbueretur. Cujus quidem instituti, nisi hallucinor, hæc est ratio, quod paulatim ad majora veniendum judicarent, &, in sacris quoque divinisque rebus, ordinem naturæ comprobarent: sive quòd indignum aliquem putarent, qui ad absoluta aut majora graduaretur sacra, nisi in minori præparatum rectè prius animum haberet. Utrisq; vero initiatum rebus omnibus florentem ac ornatum, ad extremam usq; senectutem, ac post hanc vitam, consortio Deorum, piarumque animarum insitum fore autumabant. Quod in sacris Athenienses faciendum judicabant, id in artibus & disciplinis, quibus omnis nostra vita constat, omnis nostræ ratio felicitatis continetur, quas mysteria

page.notes: The woodcut initial "A" is decorative and joined to "Thenis". Line "graf-saretur" reads as printed "graf- saretur" (likely graduaretur/ graffaretur); the word at the line end "graf-" with following "saretur" is transcribed as printed in the scan and may be misread: "graf[?]". Text continues on the next page ("ria" at the bottom right is the catchword-like fragment of the word "mysteria" split across pages; it is printed as a line-end word).
